1121-program-description: Biomedical fundamentals: cell and molecular biology and human anatomy, with experimental medicine, microbiology and immunology, pharmacology and physiology.
1121-required-courses-43-credits: A CEGEP exemption for CHEM 212, CHEM 222 or MATH 203 removes the requirement; replace those credits with electives. 3 credits from the statistics options.
1121-complementary-courses-24-credits: 12 of advanced anatomy and 12 of biologically oriented courses, 6+ at 400 level.
1122-program-description: A flexible program in cell and molecular biology and human anatomy, with biology, experimental medicine, pharmacology and neurobiology. 47 or 48 credits, by complementary choice.
1123-required-courses-32-credits: A CEGEP exemption for CHEM 212 or MATH 203 means replacing those credits with electives. 3 credits of statistics.
1123-complementary-courses-15-16-credits: 9 of advanced anatomy and 6–7 of biologically oriented courses.
1123-program-description: Register as a Major in U1. Enter Honours in U2 with CGPA 3.20, keep 3.20 at the end of U2, and graduate with 3.20. For those serious about Cell Biology careers.
1124-required-courses-52-credits: A CEGEP exemption for CHEM 212, CHEM 222 or MATH 203 means replacing those credits with electives. 3 credits of statistics.
1124-complementary-courses-21-credits: 18 of advanced anatomy and 3 of biologically oriented courses, 6+ at 400 level. ANAT 321 or ANAT 323.
1126-program-overview: Honours adds required research and advanced options for high-standing students; Major gives solid foundations. Careers in forecasting, renewable energy, reinsurance and consulting, or graduate study. The one-year Diploma is recognized by Environment and Climate Change Canada for meteorologists. Academic roles follow an M.Sc. or Ph.D.
1126-internship-year-in-science-iys: Usually between U2 and U3 (p. 1117). Available with the Major and Honours in Atmospheric Science.
1126-earth-system-science-interdepartmen: With Earth and Planetary Sciences and Geography. Contact Prof. Bruno Tremblay. See p. 1186.
1127-program-description: Physical science of the atmosphere and oceans, applied to weather and climate. 45 or 48 credits.
1127-complementary-courses-24-27-credits: Ask the Undergraduate Adviser. 3–6, then 3, 3, 3, then 12–15 from lists, 6+ of ATOC in the last.
1128-program-description: Atmospheric physics and dynamics applied to weather and climate, from chemistry to forecasting. 60–63 credits.
1128-complementary-courses-36-39-credits: Core plus one of four streams; a course counts once.
1128-core-21-22-credits: 3–6, 3, 3, 3 and 6–10 from lists. Only one each of ATOC 219 or CHEM 219, MATH 203 or 324, PHYS 340 or 350, PHYS 342 or 352.
1129-weather-analysis-and-forecasting-st: 13 and 3–4 from lists. Only one each of ATOC 404 or PHYS 404, PHYS 432 or MATH 555.
1129-climate-science-stream-15-credits: 6 and 9 from lists, 6+ of the 9 in ATOC. ATOC 404 or PHYS 404.
1130-general-stream-15-17-credits: 12+ in ATOC. Only one each of ATOC 404 or PHYS 404, PHYS 432 or MATH 555.
1130-program-description: 66–67 credits with Physics, for meteorology, atmospheric physics or related fields. See advisers in both.
1131-complementary-courses-12-13-credits: 3 and 9–10 from lists. Not both ATOC 404 and PHYS 404.
1131-program-description: 72–75 credits, with research. Enter after U1 of the Major with GPA 3.30, or from another U1 on that department's recommendation.
1132-core-24-25-credits-24-credits: 3–6, 3, 3, 3, 3 and 6–10 from lists. Only one each of ATOC 219 or CHEM 219, MATH 203 or 324, PHYS 340 or 350, PHYS 342 or 352.
1133-weather-analysis-and-forecasting-st: 16 and 6–7 from lists. PHYS 432 or MATH 555.
1133-climate-science-stream-21-22-credit: 15 and 6–7 from lists, 3 of ATOC. Only one each of ATOC 404 or PHYS 404, MATH 203 or 324, PHYS 432 or MATH 555.
1133-atmospheric-chemistry-and-physics-s: 15 and 6 from lists. Only one each of ATOC 404 or PHYS 404, PHYS 432 or MATH 555.
1134-program-description: An intensive year for B.Sc. or B.Eng. graduates in physics, applied math or similar with little meteorology, moving into atmospheric or environmental work or meeting job prerequisites. Up to 6 credits exempted for past courses, replaced by approved ones, for 30 at McGill.
1134-complementary-courses-15-credits: 6 and 9 from lists, or CHEM 519. PHYS 432 or MATH 555.
1136-about-biochemistry: Chemistry applied to biological processes in cells and molecules, since around 1900. It studies how proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, vitamins and hormones work in brain function, cell growth, signalling, inheritance and disease, and how reactions are regulated.

It underlies understanding of disease and treatment, and practical advances in medicine, veterinary work, agriculture and biotech, including protein function and genetic engineering. Specialties: neurochemistry, bioorganic, clinical, physical, molecular genetics, pharmacology and immunochemistry.

Liberal: flexible, with a minor or broader science. Major: specialized in the last two years, toward professional and research careers. Honours: adds U3 lab research; the B.Sc./M.Sc. track shortens a graduate degree. See p. 1107.

First year: lectures and labs, cell and molecular biology, and organic and physical chemistry. Then a second lab, research through BIOC 396, 462 and 491, and other complementaries. Graduates work in chemical and pharmaceutical R&D, government and hospital labs and management, or go on to research and teaching.
1137-interdepartmental-honours-in-immuno: With Microbiology and Immunology, and Physiology (p. 1203). Contact Prof. Judith Mandl, Prof. Heather Melichar or Prof. Anastasia Nyzhnyk.
1137-location: McIntyre Medical Building, 3655 Promenade Sir-William-Osler, Room 905, H3G 1Y6.
1137-u1-required-courses-20-24-credits: CEGEP credit for CHEM 242: take an elective instead.
1137-u1-complementary-courses-6-credits: 6 credits; may be moved later to fit your breadth component.
1137-u2-complementary-courses-3-credits: 3 credits; may be moved later to fit your breadth component.
1138-program-description: You may transfer in any time once requirements are met.
1138-u1-required-courses-20-24-credits: CEGEP credit for CHEM 212's equivalent: take a 3-credit elective instead.
1139-u3-complementary-courses-6-credits: 3–6 from the first list; BIOC 462 is worth 6 credits but counts as 3 toward this. Any rest from the second list.
1139-program-description: Admission only at U2. Follow U1 Major with GPA 3.20 and B- or better in all required courses, and ask undergrad.biochem@mcgill.ca during September add/drop of second year. U3 needs the same in U2; BIOC 311 and 312 matter most in close cases. Graduate with 90+ credits, no required grade under B-, and CGPA 3.20.
1140-u3-complementary-courses-6-credits: 3–6 from the first list, and any rest from the second.
